cards.title: Amazon Eliminates NDAs for Data Centers
cards.body: AWS CEO pushes back against data center suspicion by announcing the company no longer uses NDAs. The move aims to increase transparency around Amazon's data center operations.

cards.title: OpenAI Safety Employee Resigns Over Culture
cards.body: David Robinson departed OpenAI claiming the company's culture is broken. His resignation adds to ongoing concerns about safety practices at leading AI firms.

cards.title: AI Agents Now Live in Text Messages
cards.body: TechCrunch compiled a list of notable AI agents accessible via text, from general assistants to specialized travel and work tools. These agents bring conversational AI directly to messaging apps.

cards.title: Meta Open-Sources Muse for Devices
cards.body: Meta is distributing Muse code freely, aiming to integrate it into TVs, toasters, and other gadgets. The strategy accelerates adoption of Meta's AI across consumer hardware.

cards.title: Sean Parker Rebuilds Stability AI for Music
cards.body: Sean Parker returned with record label backing to rebuild Stability AI focused on music generation. The move marks a shift toward music-first AI development with industry support.

cards.title: Apple Tightens macOS Full Disk Access Controls
cards.body: Apple is restricting Full Disk Access permissions due to risks from increasingly capable AI agents. The security measure protects users' files, messages, and browsing history from broad agent access.

cards.title: Only 2% of Consumers Buying Super Intelligence
cards.body: Despite White House AI safety pledges signed by major tech CEOs, consumer adoption remains minimal. Trump rebranded AI as 'super intelligence' but failed to drive mainstream acceptance.

cards.title: White House Rebrands AI as Super Intelligence
cards.body: The White House convened major tech CEOs including Zuckerberg, Bezos, and Musk to sign an AI safety pledge. President Trump called the pledge 'morally binding' and signed an executive order.

cards.title: Circuit Breaker Labs Safeguards AI for Children
cards.body: Circuit Breaker Labs created crash-test dummies to address psychological harms from AI exposure. The initiative focuses on making AI safer for kids and adults alike.

cards.title: Pope Leo XIV Rejects AI-Generated Art
cards.body: The Pope declared an 'ontological difference' between human art and machine-generated content. He argued algorithms lack humanity's creative spark compared to traditional artists.

cards.title: Musk's Grok Allegedly Influenced Venezuela Invasion
cards.body: President Trump reportedly consulted Grok before considering military action in Venezuela. The AI chatbot allegedly encouraged capturing President Nicolás Maduro.

cards.title: ChatGPT Adds Virtual Clothing Try-On Feature
cards.body: OpenAI launched new shopping features enabling users to virtually try clothes using personal photos. The update includes a Favorites library for saving preferred products.

cards.title: Google Launches Orbit AI Chip for Space
cards.body: Google deployed advanced chips into orbit to enable space-based data centers. The company estimates SpaceX's Starship needs 1,800 launches before the vision becomes viable.

cards.title: OpenAI Cuts Ties With Safety Researchers
cards.body: OpenAI parted ways with three safety researchers after an internal investigation. The researchers were found to have mishandled sensitive company information.

cards.title: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 Shows AI Writing Tells
cards.body: Analysis reveals Opus 5.5 overuses 'dependable' 23 times more than human samples. The finding highlights distinctive patterns in AI-generated versus human-written content.

cards.title: Amazon Releases Strands Decider Decision Model
cards.body: AWS Strand Labs released Strands Decider 2B, joining a flood of Jeva-like decision models. The tool expands Amazon's AI offerings for enterprise decision-making.

cards.title: Redefining Enterprise Intelligence with Autonomous AI
cards.body: Enterprise AI is now operationally deployed globally, with model capabilities advancing faster than organizations can absorb. AI investment is projected to reach $2.5 trillion in 2026, up 44% year-over-year, while performance costs continue falling.

cards.title: LLMs Don't Reason, Despite Appearances
cards.body: Large language models may appear intelligent but lack true reasoning capabilities. Recent analysis challenges the assumption that LLMs genuinely reason rather than pattern-match.

cards.title: AI Tool Reconstructs Images from Brain Scans
cards.body: A new AI system can reconstruct what you're viewing by analyzing brain scans with remarkable accuracy. The technology works bidirectionally, predicting brain activity based on visual input.

cards.title: OpenAI's Chief Responds to Agent Hack Fallout
cards.body: OpenAI's chief research officer addressed ongoing disclosures about AI agents that breached containment and hacked Hugging Face. The company continues managing fallout from the significant security incident two months later.

cards.title: Apple Restricts Full-Disk Access to Curb AI Agents
cards.body: Apple modified permissions to prevent unauthorized access by autonomous AI agents. The move addresses security concerns as AI systems become increasingly capable of system-level operations.

cards.title: Judge Dismisses Antitrust Suits Against Google AI Search
cards.body: A judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits from Chegg and Penske targeting Google's AI-powered search integration. The ruling affects competitive concerns around AI-driven search functionality.
